title: Microfix Pulse: scheduler and compact notes
content:
Overview:

This is a compact operational note for the Microfix Pulse — our lightweight hotfix/hotpatch cadence for low-risk fixes that still need operator coordination, fast verification, and clear release notes. Purpose: make a repeatable, minimal checklist + 3-hour rollout window template so small fixes don't require a full launch runbook.

When to use Microfix Pulse:
- Priority: P2 regressions, small config fixes, critical telemetry toggles, tiled model weight swap that is backward-compatible.
- Not for: schema changes, infra migrations, database migrations, anything requiring infra changes to multiple services.

Goals for a Pulse:
- Deploy in a single 3-hour window with one rollback threshold and 15-minute verification cadence.
- Keep blast radius small (canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), preferably region-scoped.
- Produce a compact ‘release note blurb’ for customers and internal ops digest.

Preflight (before scheduling):
- PRs merged, CI green (unit + smoke), infra changes reviewed (if any).
- Owner assigned (primary) + backup on-call. Owner: Aisha P. Backup: Marco C.
- Verify zero-downtime toggle exists or flag path for fast revert.
- Telemetry: ensure synthetic queries and two alert hooks are active.
- Linked artifacts present in ticket: REL-4123 updated with final checklist and rollback criteria.
- Stakeholders notified: #release-ops, SRE, product (if customer visible).

Compact checklist (tick boxes):
- [ ] Cut branch and tag (hotfix/x.y.z-micro-N)
- [ ] Build image + push to registry (sha, tag recorded)
- [ ] Canary config prepared (route 1% to canary)
- [ ] Infra toggles / feature flag prepped (default off until canary ok)
- [ ] Smoke test harness updated with canary endpoint
- [ ] Post-deploy synthetic run created (10 queries, 95th p90 target)
- [ ] Observability bookmarks (Grafana + traces) saved and shared
- [ ] Slack run channel created: #microfix-rel-REL-4123
- [ ] Release note blurb drafted (internal + external variants)

3-hour Pulse timeline (template):
- T-60m: Final sync with stakeholders, confirm PRs, run preflight smoke locally.
- T-30m: Build + image push completed. Update REL ticket with image sha. Create canary config.
- T: Deploy canary (1% traffic). Start 15m verification cadence.
  - T+15: Check success criteria (latency, error rate, logs). If fail -> rollback.
  - T+30: If green, bump to 10% canary.
  - T+45: Check again; if green, bump to 50% (region-specific decision).
  - T+75: Full rollout to 100% if stable. If any step trips thresholds, rollback immediately.

Success/Failure thresholds (keep simple):
- Error rate increase: >2x baseline for 5m -> fail.
- Latency tail (p95) degradation: >30% above baseline for 5m -> fail.
- User-impacting errors (customer-facing 5xx) >0.2% of requests -> fail.

Smoke tests (runbook):
- Canary smoke list (quick):
  1) healthcheck /health -> 200, <200ms
  2) typical text-generation query -> response within p95 target
  3) token accounting sanity check -> cost metrics unchanged
  4) authentication/authorization check -> token refresh path
  5) simple embed request (if applicable) -> vector length OK
- Synthetic script: ./ci/smoke/microfix_canary.sh --endpoint ${CANARY_URL} --queries 10 
- Manual quick checks: traces for sample requests, logs for unusual error codes, check KV cache hit ratios.

Rollback playbook (fast):
- Owner triggers rollback if thresholds breached OR manual judgement. Steps:
  1) Disable canary flag (turn off new image routing).
  2) Re-route traffic to previous tag (record time + sha).
  3) Open a rollback note in REL ticket with timeline + owner.
  4) Post-mortem trigger if rollback required (postmortem-lite if >30m outage).

Release notes (compact draft) - external blurb (customer-facing):
- Title: "Hotfix: improved response stability in text generation (Sept 2026)"
- Body: "We deployed a targeted fix to improve stability for some text-generation workloads. The change reduces rare 5xx errors for short-context requests and should be transparent to most users. No action required. Contact support if you see regressions."

Internal release note (ops digest):
- REL-4123: Microfix deployed 2026-09-14 17:10 UTC by Aisha P. Canary -> 1% at 17:00, 10% at 17:30, 100% at 18:15. Image: registry.redwood/serving:v2026-09-14-hotfix-1887 (sha: abc123def). No rollback needed. Monitored windows: 1h post-100% with synthetic job.

Staffing & communication notes:
- Minimum headcount: owner + one SRE + one on-call dev.
- If window crosses midnight for any region, escalate staffing to 2x SRE.
- Use the microfix run channel for live logs and bookmarks. Keep messages short: status updates at each step (canary, 10%, 50%, 100%).

Post-deploy checklist (after 100%):
- [ ] Keep synthetic runs for 60 minutes
- [ ] Confirm no elevated alerts in PagerDuty for 60 minutes
- [ ] Update REL ticket with final blurb and attach smoke logs
- [ ] Close the microfix Slack channel after 2h if everything stable
- [ ] Tag the deployed image in the release registry with final note

Postmortem triggers (auto):
- Any rollback -> full postmortem-lite
- Customer-visible incident (P1/P2) during or after window -> full postmortem

Notes to self / open items:
- TODO: make a helper script that automates canary increments and rollback (ops-automation backlog).
- Q: Should we add a boolean flag in the gateway to enable instant 0% routing instead of toggling feature flag? Marco to prototype.
- Keep the pulse window configurable per-customer if the fix is customer-specific.

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Build: ./ci/build-and-push --tag hotfix-${SHORT_SHA}
- Smoke: ./ci/smoke/microfix_canary.sh --endpoint ${CANARY_URL}
- Canary routing: infra/traffic-manager set-route --service serving --tag hotfix-${TAG} --pct 1
- Logs: Grafana dashboard bookmark: ops/dashboards/microfix-canary (saved)

End of compact pulse template. Short, repeatable, and staff-light. Keep iterating; aim to reduce mean time to safe-deploy for small fixes to under 2 hours from merge to full rollout.
